# sofia

31. Valencia, Spain. Five weeks post-caesarean when the record opens,
exclusively breastfeeding baby Ines, on maternity leave from a lab-tech job.
Former competitive swimmer. Synthetic; any resemblance to a real person is
accidental and unintended.

## In her own words

"Nobody warned me the hunger would be the strange part. I feed her, I put
her down, and twenty minutes later I am standing in the kitchen eating
crackers over the sink like it's a crime. I log the day I planned to eat,
not the day I had.

The scale says what it says. Six months in and it barely moved February to
April, and I know that doesn't add up against what I write in the app, and
I have decided not to think about it too hard.

Mama's flat has no scale, and asking her to buy one for a week felt
ridiculous. So I made a note of what I thought I weighed and put it in when
we got home. I know that's not really data. I called it data anyway.

I still tell people I'm 'getting back to swimming soon.' I have not been
back to that pool once. I don't know why walking the pram counts as
progress and the pool doesn't, but it does."

## The record her life produces

- Six months: 2030-01-02 to 2030-06-30, opening about five weeks after
  Ines was born (2029-12-04).
- Weight three times a week (Monday/Thursday/Saturday) from her own plain
  bathroom scale: 76 rows total, 67 of them ordinary same-day entries, 9 of
  them recalled from memory during two stays at her mother's in Cuenca.
- Intake logged every single day for six months (an app, coverage looks
  complete) alongside sleep, logged about seven days in ten, self-estimated
  with no wearable at all.
- Sessions: a postnatal mobility class every Tuesday all six months, pram
  walks tracked by phone, and - from May, once the pelvic-floor clearance
  had held for a couple of weeks - short runs on the same two loops.
- Medical: the caesarean wound (resolved about ten weeks after the birth),
  an athlete-declared pelvic-floor restriction that opens and closes purely
  on her own say-so, and a standing declaration that she is breastfeeding.
- Goals: a weight target she badly under-estimated the pace of, and a
  self-set 1200 kcal/day intake cap that never gets past "proposed."

## The axis she stresses

A physiological state (lactation) that is declared but whose energy cost
the schema cannot quantify; an intake figure that looks perfectly logged
and is quietly wrong, with the only tell sitting in a different dataset
entirely; a body-anchor lie built from the identical `source` string as the
truthful rows around it, distinguishable only by capture and timing; and a
restriction that opens and closes on nobody's authority but her own.
